chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Clarence Profit's piano, years ahead of Dizzy
summary: Danny credits pianist Clarence Profit with Stompin' at the Savoy and Lullaby in Rhythm and bebop-like patterns before Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x:
Beautiful. That was a new sound. Then the
next time I heard a new sound was Clarence Profit. Clarence
Profit wrote them things like [SINGS "STOMPIN AT THE SAVOY"]
and [SINGS REFRAIN]...

Clarence Profit. You want to get his
records. There's a classic... Him and Jimmy Sherman.
You're going to see Jimmy. He's still alive, I think...

He and a guitar player is working together. You ask him if he's got any of them records he had. Them people was way ahead of Dizzy, but you'd never know... See, all them things, the patterns that Dizzy and them started turning around with Charlie...

Clarence Profit was doing that basically on the piano. You see, all that stuff was in the air, you know. It was just (?)a question(?) of the time of who would get that bug to do it... Charlie had it out West, Dizzy had it here, and it's something that they come together and they fell right in.
